When `externalCalendarId` is absent/undefined, the `.find()` predicate compares `cal.externalId === undefined`, which will not match normal calendar entries, so `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and the update will fall back away from the intended destination calendar. This is a real correctness issue introduced by the refactor to `destinationCalendar` being an array.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent tautological lookup: find filters cal.externalId === externalCalendarId when externalCalendarId is falsy, so selectedCalendar is undefined and events update targets wrong calendar (P1)

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts persists only destinationCalendar[0] while N destination calendars exist for collective events; 1:1 Booking→DestinationCalendar schema cannot store teammates' calendars, so reschedule/cancel leaves teammates' calendar events orphaned (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` as an array and, for COLLECTIVE team events, `handleNewBooking.ts` appends teammates’ destination calendars (`evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). However, when persisting the Booking, it still connects only the first destination calendar (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), indicating the Booking model remains effectively 1:1 with `DestinationCalendar`. The claim about orphaned teammate calendar events on reschedule/cancel is plausible but not directly verifiable from this diff because cleanup/update appears to rely on booking `references` (which were also refactored to handle multiple calendar refs), and the diff does not show how references are created for the additional destination calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Google CalendarService deleteEvent/updateEvent fallback compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId when externalCalendarId is falsy, always returning undefined; deleteEvent then defaults to 'primary' calendar, risking 404 or deleting wrong event by UID, and updateEvent never updates the real destination calendar (P1)

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute the calendar id like:

```ts
const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId
  ? externalCalendarId
  : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;
```

and similarly for `calendarId` in `deleteEvent`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (`undefined`/`null`), the `find` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` where `externalCalendarId` is that falsy value, which will almost always return no match, yielding `undefined`. In `deleteEvent`, this then falls back to `"primary"` (`calendarId: calendarId || defaultCalendarId`), meaning it may attempt to delete by UID from the wrong calendar. The same flawed selection logic applies to `updateEvent`, so it may update the wrong calendar or fall back behavior (depending on later code) rather than the actual destination calendar. This defect is directly introduced by the diff replacing the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` fallback with an always-failing `find` when `externalCalendarId` is absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Office365/Lark CalendarService createEvent always uses destination[0] ('main host') calendar, but EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent per credential with no way to select that credential's own destination, writing events to the wrong calendar for multi-host bookings (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and updates `CalendarManager.createEvent` to always call `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. However, `Office365CalendarService.createEvent` and `LarkCalendarService.createEvent` still choose the calendar via `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and use only `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (i.e., `destinationCalendar[0]`), ignoring which credential is being used. Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now loops over `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` per destination, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` does not pass that `externalId` into the calendar service—only the credential id. Result: for Office365/Lark, every loop iteration will write to the first destination calendar, causing events to be created on the wrong calendar in multi-destination/multi-host scenarios.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GoogleCalendarService.createEvent never populates externalId on its result corresponding to the selected calendar; fallback-path bookings persist references with externalCalendarId: undefined, routing them into the dead-guard delete path; dual-write between array model and legacy single-reference row is incomplete (P2)

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows a real regression in how `externalCalendarId` is carried into booking references for some create paths. `EventManager` now sets `externalCalendarId: isCalendarType ? result.externalId : undefined` (previously used `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). But `CalendarManager.createEvent` only returns `externalId` from its new optional param, and several call sites still invoke `createEvent(credential, event)` without passing an externalId (e.g., `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` branch when `destination.credentialId` is missing, and the legacy integration-type fanout path). That means created calendar references can end up with `externalCalendarId` undefined where it was previously populated from `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`, which can break later update/delete routing to the correct calendar (notably now that GoogleCalendarService uses `externalCalendarId`/`credentialId` to pick the calendar). The finding’s attribution to GoogleCalendarService not populating it is less directly shown, but the diff-grounded externalId propagation bug is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleCancelBooking.ts DB-fetch fallback uses prisma.credential.findUnique without filtering type.endsWith('_calendar') and without userId/teamId scoping, trusting reference credentialId blindly and risking deleteEvent against a non-calendar credential (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `handleCancelBooking.ts`, when a calendar reference has a `credentialId` but it isn’t found in `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`, the new fallback does `prisma.credential.findUnique({ where: { id: credentialId } })` and then calls `getCalendar(calendarCredential)` / `deleteEvent(...)` with that credential. The diff shows no scoping to `userId`/`teamId` and no validation that `foundCalendarCredential.type` is a calendar type (e.g. `endsWith('_calendar')`). Since `credentialId` is taken directly from the booking reference, this can result in using an unrelated/non-calendar credential if the reference is wrong or maliciously crafted, potentially deleting against the wrong integration/identity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:~1092 — evt.destinationCalendar?.push silently drops teamDestinationCalendars when evt.destinationCalendar is null, causing collective booking events to be created in only one calendar with no warning (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to `null` when neither `eventType.destinationCalendar` nor `organizerUser.destinationCalendar` exists (`destinationCalendar: ... : null`). Immediately after, for collective team events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. Because of the optional chaining, this becomes a no-op when destinationCalendar is null, so the collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded. This is a concrete, diff-verifiable logic error that can prevent adding team members’ destination calendars for COLLECTIVE bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarService.ts updateEvent/deleteEvent — new destinationCalendar?.find comparison never matches when externalCalendarId is falsy, leaving selectedCalendar/calendarId undefined so updates/deletes of legacy bookings fail silently (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `updateEvent` now computes `selectedCalendar` as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy/undefined (common for legacy references), the `.find(...)` predicate compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e., `=== undefined`), which will not match any real calendar externalId, leaving `selectedCalendar` undefined. That undefined is then used as `calendarId` in `calendar.events.update(...)`. The same faulty pattern is introduced for delete (`calendarId = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`), so legacy updates/deletes can break because the previous fallback (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) was removed and not replaced with a valid default (e.g., first destination calendar).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~117 — destructured mainHostDestinationCalendar without null check throws TypeError for Google Meet bookings with no destination calendar, breaking the Cal Video fallback path (P1)
matched_golden_ids: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root cause: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is destructured from `evt.destinationCalendar` without guarding against it being null/empty, leading to a TypeError when no destination calendar is present. The candidate points to a different file/location, but the underlying bug is the same missing null/empty check during destructuring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: office365calendar/larkcalendar/BaseCalendarService createEvent not updated with credentialId param; all read event.destinationCalendar[0], creating N duplicate events in host #1's calendar and none for other hosts in collective bookings (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` to an array and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents()` now loops over all `event.destinationCalendar` entries, calling `createEvent(...)` per destination (and even passing `destination.externalId` via `CalendarManager.createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`). However, `office365calendar`, `larkcalendar`, and `BaseCalendarService` were updated to always use only the first destination calendar (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`). This means when multiple destination calendars exist (e.g., COLLECTIVE adds team members’ destination calendars), each loop iteration for those integrations will still target the first calendar, potentially creating multiple duplicate events in host #1’s calendar and not creating events in other hosts’ calendars.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~549 updateAllCalendarEvents — undefined credential on failed lookup causes a throw converted to failure results for all references, mis-reporting partial failure as total failure (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents`, `calendarReference` was changed from a single ref to an array (`filter(...)`), and the code now loops all refs. Inside the loop, when `reference.credentialId` is set, it assigns `credential = this.calendarCredentials.filter(...)[0]` and tries to fetch from DB if missing — but if it still can’t be resolved, it still does `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` without guarding `credential` (so `credential` can be `undefined`, causing `updateEvent` to throw). That thrown error is caught by the outer `try/catch`, and the `catch` now returns failure results for *all* references via `calendarReference?.map(...)`, which will mis-report a partial failure (one bad/missing credential) as total failure for every reference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: handleNewBooking.ts:~1875 — only destinationCalendar[0].id is persisted as a booking reference; extra teamDestinationCalendars entries are never stored, so their calendar events become orphaned on reschedule/cancel (P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that when persisting the booking in handleNewBooking it only connects the first destination calendar (`connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`), so extra `teamDestinationCalendars` are not stored on the booking’s `destinationCalendar` relation. However, the finding claims this is persisted as a *booking reference* and that the extra calendars are “never stored” leading to orphaned events on reschedule/cancel. The diff does not show how booking calendar *references* are created/stored for the additional calendar events, and reschedule/cancel logic in this diff was explicitly changed to handle multiple `*_calendar` references (filter + loop), which suggests multi-calendar references may exist. Therefore the asserted orphaning-on-reschedule/cancel is not verifiable from this diff and the finding mischaracterizes what is persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager.ts:~380 createAllCalendarEvents DB-fetch branch — destination silently skipped when credential exists but app.slug is missing, with no log or error (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents, when a destination has credentialId but the credential isn't in this.calendarCredentials, the code fetches it from DB and only reconstructs `credential` if `credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug` (new branch in the diff). If `app.slug` is missing/null, `credential` stays undefined and the destination is skipped because event creation is guarded by `if (credential) { ... }`, with no log/error path. This can silently drop calendar event creation for that destination.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CalendarManager.ts:~230 — 404 catch returns undefined yet a result with stale externalId/credentialId is pushed into createdEvents; multi-destination loop now multiplies these swallowed failures and persists references to nonexistent events (P2, advisory)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/CalendarManager.ts#createEvent`, the 404 handler returns `undefined` only for `creationResult` (via `.catch(...) { if (error?.code === 404) return undefined; }`), but `createEvent` still returns an `EventResult` object that includes `externalId` (passed in) and `credentialId: credential.id` (added at return) regardless of success. In `packages/core/EventManager.ts#createAllCalendarEvents`, the loop pushes the returned `EventResult` unconditionally (`if (createdEvent) createdEvents.push(createdEvent);`), and since `createEvent(...)` always returns an object, failures (including swallowed 404s) will still be pushed. Downstream mapping now uses `result.externalId` / `result.credentialId` for calendar references, so this can persist references even when `result.createdEvent` is `undefined`. The new multi-destination loop increases how often this happens by repeating the pattern per destination calendar.
